result.scope: Source-only review of orchestrator/hosted_cycle_reconcile.py and tests/test_hosted_cycle_reconcile.py — non-dispatching completed-wake reconciliation (evidence verification, identity bindings, wake consumption idempotency); imported helpers (Controller, Queue, lock, identifier, encoded, finalize) reviewed only as exercised by the supplied test; no tests executed.
findings: Fail-closed ordering holds: all filesystem evidence (binding, complete, three receipts with sha256-verified stdout/stderr/input/answer, content-addressed report, queue row, byte-compared review/disposition) is verified before the state DB is opened, and the test asserts jobs.sqlite is not created on missing evidence.

Identity bindings are sound: binding pinned to event id, complete.json must agree with binding, DB event payload re-hashed via canonical encoded() against event_sha256, wake.job bound to event.job, report id is sha256 of the report file, and queue review/disposition artifacts must byte-match the receipt-hashed cycle artifacts — preserving the recorded approvals.

Recovery semantics are correct and idempotent: driver.lock plus BEGIN IMMEDIATE, duplicate accepted only when reason is SUPERVISED_CYCLE_<this report>, OTHER_CYCLE_ALREADY_PROCESSED refusal otherwise, rollback on any exception; the module never dispatches (model_calls=0, job_dispatches=0).

Advisory: actual_model is verified only for the review stage (claude-fable-5); continuation/disposition check requested_model alone, so a served-model substitution on the astra stages passes — tighten if the per-stage model plan is meant to bind all three stages.

Advisory: read_checked's REGULAR_PRIVATE_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED name overstates its guarantee — no permission/ownership check, hardlinks pass, and the symlink check is subject to a swap-after-check race (low risk under the single-writer lock).

Advisory: Controller is constructed after evidence checks, so valid evidence with a missing/foreign state DB creates an empty jobs.sqlite before refusing with TRIGGER_EVENT_CHANGED — a benign persistent artifact on a refusal path.

Caveat: receipts are unauthenticated (the test fabricates a passing fixture), so the checks defend against corruption/drift within a trusted destination folder rather than an adversary with write access; this matches the apparent trust model.
